newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU likely to propose Vienna ends ban on gene maize.
newsitem.headline: EU likely to propose Vienna ends ban on gene maize.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it was likely to propose later this month that Austria should end its ban on imports of genetically modified maize.

Environment spokesman Peter Joergensen told a news briefing that three EU scientific committees had not found any new information to go against the Commission's decision last December to clear imports of the modified maize.
"The Commission will act on the scientific advice," Joergensen said, adding it would present a proposal in the next two weeks.
Austria, worried by health risks, last December unilaterally banned imports of the maize, which is resistant to the herbicide gluphosinate and the corn-borer pest.
The maize was developed by Ciba-Geigy and marketed by Swiss company Novartis.

EU member states will have 28 days to decide by weighted majority whether to approve the Commission's proposal. If they are unable to reach such a majority then a final decision could be delayed until September, Joergensen said.
